title: ÆTHER: Sway v7 (refined: hook, transitions, flow)
story: Two young people on their first evening walk by the sea: one hook that keeps coming back, each time closer.
script:
# Sway v7: scene script (written before the music)

**Moment:** two young people on their first evening walk by the sea, soft and happy. **Length:** 80 s. **Key/tempo:** A major (Shankarabharanam), 120 BPM, one steady groove.
**Main idea:** one hook that keeps coming back, each time a little closer to them. Every section change is a walking step, never a stop.

| Time | On screen | What the music does |
|---|---|---|
| 0-8 s | Sunset, waves, she turns and smiles. | The HOOK at once: the female hum sings the 2-bar hook, flute doubles it; light tabla and Rhodes, groove already moving. |
| 8-16 s | They start walking side by side. | Groove fills out (bass, soft kick, guitar strum); the tumbi and synth pluck answer the hook. |
| 15-16 s | A wave splashes their feet. | TRANSITION: one-bar tabla roll + rising santoor run into the next part, no stop. |
| 16-32 s | They laugh, shy glances. | The hook again on flute, the male hum answers each phrase; the same four-chord loop (A, F#m, D, E). |
| 31-32 s | She takes his hand. | TRANSITION: dholak pickup + soft cymbal swell into the lift. |
| 32-48 s | Walking hand in hand, the lights come on along the shore. | Middle part: violin and santoor play a variation of the hook (same rhythm, higher), hums in harmony; groove a little busier. |
| 47-48 s | They stop at the water's edge. | TRANSITION: two-beat tabla fill + hum glide back into the hook. |
| 48-72 s | Closest moment, foreheads touch, laughter. | The hook at its fullest: female and male hum together with flute and strings, everything playing. |
| 72-80 s | Wide shot, two silhouettes, the sea. | The hook one last time on the female hum alone over light tabla, ending on a clean A. |

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 09:35-12:12: v5 take 2 is the right track (romantic, not refreshing), wants professional humming, and 'more refinement: transition, and flows in music, hooks'. v7 keeps v5 take 2's identity (A major, 120 BPM, one band, one hook) and adds what he asked: a short singable 2-bar hook from second 0 returning every section, a fixed four-chord loop so the harmony flows, and a one-bar fill into every section change (never a stop). Pro playback-singer humming built in (v6's plain hum sounded amateur). Raga Shankarabharanam on A (v5 take 2 measured only 64% in raga, chromatic). Script-first per music-scoring rule 17. Prompt mode (music_v2).

prompt: ONE SONG, ONE HOOK, SMOOTH FLOW: a warm, tender, gently uplifting romantic song with wordless humming only, no lyrics, in the style of modern South Indian film music, for two young people on their first evening walk by the sea. A major the whole time, raga Shankarabharanam (the A major scale A B C# D E F# G# with Carnatic gamakam shakes on C#, F# and G#), exactly 120 BPM with a light lilting swing; the beat and the groove never stop from the first second to the last. THE HOOK: a short, simple, singable two-bar melody, instantly memorable, heard in the very first bar, and it keeps coming back in every section so the whole track is built on it. THE HARMONY FLOWS: the same warm four-chord loop (A major, F sharp minor, D major, E major) repeats under the whole song. TRANSITIONS: every change of section is led in by a one-bar tabla roll or dholak pickup with a rising santoor run or soft cymbal swell, so each part grows out of the last one, never a stop, never a gap, never a sudden new sound. THE VOICES: a world-class professional female playback singer, Carnatic-trained, hums the hook (soft mmm opening into a sweet aah), effortless, perfectly in tune, expressive, with graceful slides, quick grace-note turns and delicate vibrato on long notes, close and polished; a warm, skilled male voice hums the answers. THE BAND (the same all the way through): bamboo flute doubling the hook, a bright tumbi and a bouncy synth pluck answering it, solo violin, santoor, mandolin and clean electric guitar strumming lightly, warm Rhodes, a soft arpeggiator, tabla and dholak with a soft modern kick, light snaps and a deep round bass. Acoustic instruments and voices sound natural, dry and close, no echo or delay on them, never chopped or reversed. Timeline: 0-8 s the female voice sings the hook at once with flute, light tabla and Rhodes already in the groove. 8-16 s the groove fills out with bass, soft kick and guitar; tumbi and synth pluck answer the hook. 15-16 s a one-bar tabla roll and rising santoor run lead in. 16-32 s the hook on flute, the male voice answers each phrase. 31-32 s a dholak pickup and soft cymbal swell. 32-48 s violin and santoor play a higher variation of the hook, the voices in harmony, the groove a little busier. 47-48 s a short tabla fill and a voice glide lead back. 48-72 s the hook at its fullest: both voices with flute and warm strings, everything playing. 72-80 s the female voice sings the hook one last time over light tabla, ending on a clean A. Not a movie background, no big orchestral swells, no choir, no new unrelated melodies, no breaks, no EDM drop, no side-chain pumping, no silence anywhere.
